title: Nilo-Saharan languages - Wikipedia
text: The Nilo-Saharan languages are a proposed linguistic family consisting of around 210 Native African languages spoken by somewhere around 70 million speakers, mainly in the upper parts of the Chari and Nile rivers, including historic Nubia, north of where the two tributaries of the Nile meet.

text: Le dongotono, comme de nombreuses langues nilo-sahariennes, différencie les voyelles selon leur lieu d'articulation. Elles sont soit prononcées avec l'avancement de la racine de la langue, soit avec la rétraction de la racine de la langue[6].

title: Dongotono language | Laskon Wiki | Fandom
text: Dongotono is an Eastern Nilotic language spoken by an estimated 5,000 people in South Sudan. There has been very little research on Dongotono, but some tentative phonological and morphological observations can be found in Vossen (1982), based on wordlist data collected in the 1970s.

title: Dongotono language — Grokipedia
text: The Dongotono language (also known as Dɔngɔtɔnɔ) is an Eastern Nilotic language (ISO 639-3: ddd) belonging to the Nilo-Saharan language family, spoken by approximately 5,000 people primarily in Ik.
